text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Minister of Justice Sevket Kazan asks for legal action against general Osman Ozbek who harshly criticised Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
- More than 160 people were killed and another 415 were injured in car accidents in a week-long holiday.

- Education Minister Mehmet Saglam says that Islamist premier Erbakan opposes implementing eight years of uninterrupted compulsory education, which Erbakan's Welfare Party says will effectively close down religious schools.
- A defender of the Islamic Sharia law, known as "Ali Hodja", trains teams in Istanbul to murder in the name of Islamic Jihad.
- Erbakan openly opposes eight-year uninterrupted compulsory education.

- The conservative coalition partner has begun preparing an early election calender. The opposition is exploring new government formulae ahead of a critical regular meeting of a top military-government board.
- Recent political turmoil is an obstacle to the implementation of long-term reforms in the economy.
- The Turkish armed forces killed 36 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) militants in a day of operations held in the mainly- Kurdish southeast.
